rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 8 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window without risking truncation. The wide phi range and moderate slope should reveal whether retention is concentrated early, late, or across the full gradient.

All peaks elute between about phi_e 0.20 and 0.44, so trimming the gradient window around the observed elution region should increase effective selectivity and may open the unresolved 4/5 pair while keeping all compounds inside the gradient. Keep tG and T fixed to isolate the effect of narrowing the phi window.

The narrow window greatly improved the critical 4/5 pair, so now test whether shortening the gradient can pull t_last back under 10 min while preserving enough selectivity. This directly probes whether the remaining limitation is mainly slope-sensitive or if the pair is already close to its best at this phi window.

The critical pair improves with the narrow window but collapses when the slope is made steeper, suggesting it is not purely slope-limited and may need a selectivity change. Lowering temperature at the successful 0.25–0.45, 20 min method is a clean way to test whether the 4/5 pair can be reordered or spread further without changing the useful phi window.

Lowering T hurt badly and shifted the critical behavior, so try the opposite extreme at the same promising phi window and slope. Higher temperature may alter selectivity enough to improve the troublesome close pair while also reducing the time penalty.

The 0.25–0.45 window improved one close pair but introduced different crowding at the temperature extremes, suggesting the window may be too tight and forcing multiple compounds into the same local selectivity region. A slightly wider, still focused window centered on the observed elution range should test whether modestly reducing compression can improve the worst pair without sacrificing full elution.

This window fully resolves all pairs, so the remaining objective is to reduce t_last toward 10 min. Shortening tG one step should test how much time can be saved before the first pair drops below baseline full-credit resolution.

At 0.20–0.50 and 20 min all pairs are fully resolved, so the next lever is temperature to shorten retention without steepening the gradient enough to recreate the close pairs seen at 16 min. A modest +5 C change is safer than jumping to 60 C, which previously changed selectivity too much.

The 45 C run improved CRF despite one slightly sub-1.5 pair, so a small increase in phi1 should selectively accelerate the later compounds and reduce the time penalty while leaving the early crowded region, where the weak pair sits, nearly unchanged. This is a cleaner way to chase t_last than further increasing temperature or steepening the whole gradient.

The remaining deficit is a single early pair around rows 3/4, while the time penalty is already small. Lowering phi0 one step should expand the low-phi portion where that early pair elutes and may raise its resolution above 1.5, with only a modest increase in retention for the last peak.

Raising phi1 from 0.50 to 0.55 improved CRF mainly by shortening the late end while leaving the critical 3/4 pair almost unchanged, so one more step in phi1 is the logical exploitation move. This should further reduce t_last with minimal impact on the early selectivity bottleneck.

The current best has no time penalty and only one slightly sub-threshold pair, and previous increases in phi1 mainly shortened the late peaks while leaving the critical early 3/4 pair almost unchanged. One more step up in phi1 may improve CRF further by keeping t_last safely below 10 min without materially worsening the limiting pair.

The best point so far is 0.20–0.60, 20 min, 45 C; increasing phi1 further compressed a later pair, so keep the successful window and test a small temperature increase instead. This may shift selectivity enough to improve the persistent 3/4 pair while likely keeping t_last under 10 min.

The persistent limiting pair is highly temperature-sensitive but has stayed near the same place at 45 C, so the safer next lever is a slightly shallower gradient at the current best window and temperature. Extending tG by one step should test whether the 3/4 pair is still slope-responsive enough to reach full credit, while the expected small time penalty may still leave CRF competitive if it does.

The stubborn 3/4 pair is essentially insensitive to tG near the best conditions, so changing the phi window shape is more promising than further slope changes. Raising phi0 while keeping phi1 at 0.60 should shift more gradient span to the region where the critical early pair elutes and may improve its selectivity while preserving the excellent t_last.

The best method is 0.20–0.60, 20 min, 45 C, and both higher and lower nearby temperatures have caused major selectivity shifts; to map that behavior more completely, test the other side of 45 C. A drop to 35 C may improve the stubborn 3/4 pair without the extreme changes seen at 25 C, though with some increase in retention.

At the best conditions, the only deficit is a single pair at R 1.22 while t_last is just under 10 min, so there may be room to shorten the run slightly and gain time without much loss in pair credit. The 3/4 pair appears selectivity-limited near 45 C and 0.20–0.60, while 40 C with a narrower upper bound previously gave a fully resolved chromatogram. Testing 0.15–0.60 at 40 C explores a cooler, broader low-phi window that may open the early critical pair enough to exceed 1.5, even at the cost of some retention increase.

This probes whether a modestly narrower high-phi window can keep both critical regions acceptable and beat the current best on overall CRF.

The critical 3/4 pair has resisted changes in slope and phi window near the optimum, indicating a selectivity problem, so with only a few injections left it is worth probing the remaining untested temperature on the cooler side. Thirty degrees may separate that pair differently than 35 or 25 C while keeping retention less severe than the 25 C run.

This tests whether the selectivity regime seen at 30 C can be exploited into a higher CRF than the current best.

The 45 C, 0.20–0.60, 20 min method is still best, but temperatures around it have caused dramatic selectivity changes; with two shots left, the only realistic chance to beat 0.973 is a favorable temperature-induced reordering while keeping the proven window and no time penalty. At 55 C the limiting pair is again the early 3/4 region, while the late end has ample time margin; lowering phi1 one step should ease the gradient in the early-middle region and may improve that pair without introducing a time penalty. This is the last nearby unexplored combination with a plausible chance to beat the current best by nudging the stubborn pair upward while keeping t_last near 10 min.
